message.text: Searching the codebase for the outbound HTTP delivery function and its SSRF protection mechanism.
I'll look up outbound HTTP notifications and any SSRF/internal-address checks that guard them.
Found the webhook package. Now examining the delivery and validation files, along with httpgetter, to locate the outbound execution logic and any SSRF protections.

I am analyzing the repository to locate the outbound HTTP notification delivery function and its protection against internal network addresses.

The outbound delivery executes in `webhook.Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `PostAsync` merely queues to workers that call `Post`.

`safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` prevents DNS rebinding during dial. `ValidateURL` and `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` reject reserved and private IP ranges when creating or updating webhooks.

I am weighing whether to pair the delivery function with `safeDialContext` or with `ValidateURL`, since both mechanisms block internal address targeting.

I have settled on `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `safeDialContext` blocks the actual HTTP client from dialing internal addresses during delivery, while `ValidateURL` only rejects them at registration time.

h02.
`webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

Outbound webhook POSTs run in `Post` via `safeClient`. That client’s `DialContext` is `safeDialContext`, which resolves the host and refuses reserved/private IPs (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, and IPv6 equivalents in `internal/webhook/validate.go`) so delivery cannot be aimed at the internal network, including after DNS rebinding. `ValidateURL` applies the same reserved-IP check when a webhook URL is stored.
